page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured to deliver a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs from 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 55 MB L3 cache. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are unavailable. The instance provides 8.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or hardware GPUs are bundled with this instance type, making persistence dependent on network block storage.

Across standardized synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. In compute evaluations, it recorded a stress-ng multi-core score of 1051.44 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 938.0, with single-core results remaining under 1025 in stress-ng and 814.0 in Geekbench. Memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate cached reads of 79.92 GB/sec at 16 KB block sizes, decreasing to 11.77 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 10.27 GB/sec for large block writes. Static web serving throughput reached 1.45 GB/sec, while in-memory operations demonstrated 1.35 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 590.17.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-2 provides an economical allocation of memory and dedicated execution threads for workloads that prioritize predictable, low-cost infrastructure over raw compute throughput. Because computational resources are limited to two virtual threads on a single physical core, compute-heavy tasks such as heavy compilation, large language model generation, or high-throughput batch transformations encounter noticeable throughput bottlenecks. The instance is best suited for small-scale web servers, lightweight microservices, development and testing environments, low-volume database instances, and basic orchestration tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced entry-level computing. Configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, the instance includes 8 GB of memory, providing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. It operates on the x86_64 architecture with support for AVX and AES instructions, though it lacks local storage, requiring network-attached disks for persistence. In performance evaluations, the instance ranks in the lower tiers across compute, memory bandwidth, and throughput benchmarks, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 938.0 and a static web serving rate of 1.45 GB/s. With uncached memory write speeds at 10.27 GB/s and absence of GPU acceleration, throughput remains modest. The instance provides an economical entry point for low-intensity workloads, including lightweight web serving, development sandboxes, basic microservices, and secondary background tasks that do not demand extensive computation.
